question.problem:
On average, $53%$ of the emails Emily receives are spam. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, estimate the probability that she has $70$ or more spam emails in her inbox if she has $140$ emails in her inbox. Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1841\,$ | $\,0.1814\,$ | $\,0.1788\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2119\,$ | $\,0.2090\,$ | $\,0.2061\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=140$ and $p=0.53.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =140\cdot 0.53 \\  & =74.2 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =140\cdot (1-0.53) \\  & =65.8 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(140)(0.53)=74.2
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(140)(0.53)(1-0.53)=34.874.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(74.2,34.874).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X\ge 70).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X\ge 70)≈P(Y\ge 69.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 69.5) & =1-P(Y<69.5) \\  & =1-P(Z<\frac{69.5-74.2}{\sqrt{34.874}}) \\  & ≈1-P(Z<-0.80) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.80) \\  & =1-0.2119 \\  & =0.7881\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X\ge 70)≈0.788.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.7869.$
